2: title: sk-code-quality
3: description: The post-implementation quality gate for the sk-code family. It runs the quality runner over the change, loads the checklists the verdict names, applies P0/P1/P2 author checks and hands only clean evidence to verification.
4: trigger_phrases:
5:   - "quality gate"
6:   - "code quality"
7:   - "comment hygiene"
8:   - "authoring checklist"
9: importance_tier: important
10: contextType: implementation
11: version: 1.3.7.0
12: ---
13: 
14: # sk-code-quality
15: 
16: > Implementation can be behaviorally close and still not shippable. This mode runs the author-side quality gate after files change and before verification, so gate failures are fixed in place and only clean evidence reaches the surface verification workflow.
17: 
18: ---
19: 
20: ## 1. AT A GLANCE
21: 
22: | Aspect | What you get |
23: |---|---|
24: | **Use it for** | Post-implementation quality checks, P0/P1/P2 author-side fixes, comment hygiene and OpenCode target-path checklists |
25: | **Invoke with** | `quality gate`, `code quality`, `comment hygiene`, `authoring checklist`, `check before done` |
26: | **Works on** | Any repository: the runner checks the change with the universal floor and the checks the repository names. In this repository it also loads the SKILLED checklists for skills, agents, commands, specs, MCP servers, scripts, config and language files |
27: | **Produces** | In-place quality fixes plus a handoff that states the runner's verdict, the checklists used, the hygiene rules switched off and any remaining risk |
28: 
29: ---
30: 
31: ## 2. OVERVIEW
32: 
33: ### Why This Mode Exists
34: 
35: Implementation can produce code that is behaviorally close and still not shippable: a forbidden comment label, a missing authoring checklist, stale generated output, a style violation or a P0 quality defect that verification would not explain well. The quality mode closes that gap before final evidence is collected.
36: 
37: ### What It Does
38: 
39: The quality mode runs `scripts/quality-gate.cjs` over the change, which works in any repository. The runner's verdict names the gate, the state of each enforcement layer and the checklists that apply. The mode loads those checklists and applies P0/P1/P2 author checks. It can edit existing scoped files to fix gate failures in place. It does not create new files, dispatch tasks, produce formal review reports or make done claims.
40: 
41: ### The Checklist Router
42: 
43: The mode's headline strength is routing by target path: every surface family lands on the checklist that covers it, so the gate checks the same things a human reviewer would check. The universal floor applies to every file. The rows below are this hub's own SKILLED surface, which loads for files the surface detection places in it.
44: 
45: | Target family | What the mode knows how to check |
46: |---|---|
47: | **OpenCode skills** | loads the skill-authoring checklist by target path |
48: | **OpenCode agents and commands** | routes to the agent-authoring and command-authoring checklists |
49: | **Spec folders** | routes to the spec-folder authoring checklist that `system-spec-kit` owns |
50: | **MCP servers** | routes to the MCP-server-authoring checklist |
51: | **Language files and config** | applies the language-specific and config checklists |
52: | **Your own surface** | a surface another skill declares, or a checklist your `.skilled/skills/sk-code/sk-code-quality/repository/quality.json` names, brings its own checklists |
53: 
54: ---
55: 
56: ## 3. QUICK START
57: 
58: **Step 1: Route after implementation.** Use this mode after the surface skill (`sk-code-skilled`) has changed files and before the surface verification workflow (`workflow-verify.md`) collects final evidence.
59: 
60: **Step 2: Run the quality runner.**
61: 
62: ```bash
63: node .skilled/skills/sk-code/sk-code-quality/scripts/quality-gate.cjs --format text
64: ```
65: 
66: The runner reads the change, by default the working tree against `HEAD`. It runs the conflict-marker, secret and debug-leftover sensors, one comment-hygiene call over the changed files and a parse floor, and probes which hooks and workflows enforce hygiene. It prints one verdict with a gate and an exit code from 0 to 4. No gate means pass: exit 0 says only that no blocker was found and that every required check produced evidence. [`references/runner-contract.md`](./references/runner-contract.md) documents every field. A committed `.skilled/skills/sk-code/sk-code-quality/repository/quality.json` runs its commands only in a trusted repository. Without a grant each configured check reads `SKIPPED_UNTRUSTED` with the repair `git config --local skilled.trustRepoChecks true`, and [section 8 of the quality config reference](./references/quality-config.md) names the grants.
67: 
68: **Step 3: Load the checklists the verdict names.** The universal floor [`code-quality-standards.md`](../shared/references/universal/code-quality-standards.md) loads for every target. It gives each rule an id and marks it FIXED or overridable. [`universal-checklist.md`](../sk-code-skilled/assets/checklists/universal-checklist.md) is the SKILLED house checklist, and it loads only when SKILLED is a resolved surface. On SKILLED it also names the JavaScript and CSS house checks for a `.js` or `.css` target, in [`js-css-style/`](../sk-code-skilled/assets/checklists/js-css-style/). For `.skilled/` targets it names the matching checklist under [`../sk-code-skilled/assets/checklists/`](../sk-code-skilled/assets/checklists/). The house style of this framework (file layout, `MODULE:` headers, the `ceiling:` marker, test layout) lives in those SKILLED files, so another repository does not inherit it.
69: 
70: **Step 4: Fix or hand back.** Fix in-place quality failures with `Edit`. Root-cause failures that need investigation to the surface debugging workflow (`workflow-debug.md`). Send final evidence to the surface verification workflow (`workflow-verify.md`).
71: 
72: ---
73: 
74: ## 4. HOW IT WORKS
75: 
76: The mode sits between implementation and verification. It runs the quality runner over the changed files, which resolves surface identity through the shared surface reader and names the checklists that apply. The mode loads them and checks P0/P1/P2 status. P0 blocks completion. P1 is fixed unless the user accepts a documented risk. P2 is fixed when cheap or explicitly deferred with a reason.
77: 
78: ### The P0/P1/P2 Gate
79: 
80: | Severity | Meaning | Gate effect |
81: |---|---|---|
82: | **P0** | Correctness, safety, broken contract, forbidden comment metadata, unchecked generated drift or missing checklist evidence | Blocks completion until fixed or escalated |
83: | **P1** | Maintainability or authoring-contract issue that would confuse future work | Fixed before handoff unless the user accepts a documented risk |
84: | **P2** | Local polish or minor consistency issue with low behavioral risk | Fixed when cheap, otherwise deferred with a documented reason |
85: 
86: ### Target-Path Routing
87: 
88: OpenCode authoring targets route to specific checklists: skills, agents, commands, MCP servers, language files and config each have their own checklist under `sk-code-skilled`. Spec folders route to the spec-folder authoring checklist that `system-spec-kit` owns. `node scripts/quality-gate.cjs --explain <path> [<path>...]` answers for a whole change in one call. For each file it names the surfaces, the folder each surface loads from and every checklist with the seat that declared it, plus each checklist's parsed `## Rule overrides` rows. It runs nothing and writes nothing. It exits 2 when every path resolves, and 3 (ERROR) on a usage error or a missing path.
89: 
90: ### Rules Your Repository Can Change
91: 
92: The universal floor splits into FIXED rules and overridable ones. The hard floor stays on in every repository: secrets, conflict markers, parse failures, input validation, silent failures, initialization safety, resource cleanup and accessibility for UI code. A repository can drop or replace the rest, such as documentation, typing strictness, naming and the `ceiling:` marker.
93: 
94: There are two ways to say so, and they work together.
95: 
96: - **A `## Rule overrides` section** in a checklist the repository already declares, such as one named in `.skilled/skills/sk-code/sk-code-quality/repository/quality.json` `checklists[]`. Each row gives a rule id, `none` or `replace: <text>` and an optional reason. The shared contract is [`rule-overrides.md`](../shared/references/universal/rule-overrides.md), and `node ../shared/scripts/check-rule-overrides.cjs <checklist.md>` checks a section. A row that names a hard-floor id is refused.
97: - **`commentHygiene.disableRules`** in `.skilled/skills/sk-code/sk-code-quality/repository/quality.json` switches off named core comment-hygiene rules, such as `issue` or `task`. The runner, the pre-commit hook and the CI job all honor it, and the verdict lists what is off in `config.hygiene.disabled`. An unknown id, or a hard-floor id such as `secret.private-key`, is `CONFIG_INVALID`.
98: 
99: A run reads the section of every checklist it loads. A refused section, or a row whose rule id no declaring document carries, ends the run `ERROR` with `CONFIG_INVALID` and exit 3, and the error names the checklist and every reason. Each accepted row is recorded in `rule_overrides` and in the envelope's `p0_p1_p2_decisions` as `override <rule id> <none|replace> from <checklist>`, ahead of `PENDING_AGENT_JUDGMENT`. Two checklists at one precedence level that disagree on a rule leave its default in force, appear in `rule_conflicts` and join `summary.unverified`, so the gate reads `UNVERIFIED`.
100: 
101: A recorded hygiene row tells the agent and the review mode what to apply. The runner's own comment-hygiene check changes only through `disableRules`, so a repository that wants a hygiene rule off everywhere sets both. `--explain` shows what each checklist's section says and the conflicts for each file, and `/doctor:sk-code quality` shows the same answer for the whole repository.
102: 
103: ### The Mutation Boundary
104: 
105: This mode can edit already-scoped files because author-side quality correction is part of implementation. It cannot write new files and cannot dispatch subagents. Findings-only review belongs to `sk-code-review`.
106: 
107: ---
108: 
109: ## 5. INTEGRATION & NAVIGATION
110: 
111: ### When To Use This Mode
112: 
113: Use it when a change is already written and needs standards enforcement before final verification: skill authoring, script changes, config changes, frontend quality, comment hygiene or stale generated-output checks. Skip it when the task is to build new behavior, debug a failing symptom, verify non-mutating evidence or review without editing.
114: 
115: ### Related Skills
116: 
117: | Skill | Relationship |
118: |---|---|
119: | `sk-code` | Parent hub that routes the quality workflow here |
120: | `sk-code-skilled` | Surface skills that implement and change files, own root-cause debugging and gather verification evidence through the implement → debug → verify workflow doctrine |
121: | `sk-code-review` | Produces findings-first reports when no author-side editing is wanted |
122: 
123: ---
124: 
125: ## 6. VERIFICATION
126: 
127: | Check | How to run it |
128: |---|---|
129: | Quality verdict | `node .skilled/skills/sk-code/sk-code-quality/scripts/quality-gate.cjs` prints one `code-quality-run/v1` verdict and exits 0 to 4, as `references/runner-contract.md` section 2 states. It writes no file |
130: | Runner tests | `node --test .skilled/skills/sk-code/sk-code-quality/scripts/tests/*.test.cjs` runs the named fixtures and unit cases, each in a throwaway repository |
131: | Comment hygiene | `.skilled/skills/sk-code/sk-code-quality/scripts/check-comment-hygiene.sh <modified-file>` reports zero violations and exits 0. Run it directly, not through `bash`, because it is a Python program. Add `--disable-rule <id>` to skip one core rule |
132: | Rule overrides | `node .skilled/skills/sk-code/shared/scripts/check-rule-overrides.cjs <checklist.md>` exits 0 for a valid or absent `## Rule overrides` section and 1 when a row is refused |
133: | Distribution drift | `.skilled/skills/sk-code/sk-code-quality/scripts/check-dist-staleness.sh <changed-file>` prints a banner when the package that holds the file is stale or cannot be checked, and nothing when it is current. This per-file form never rebuilds. It always exits 0 because it warns and does not gate. Run it directly, not through `bash`, because it is a Python program |
134: | Ceiling markers | `.skilled/skills/sk-code/sk-code-quality/scripts/ceiling-report.sh` prints one line per `ceiling:` or `intentional-limit:` marker and a closing `markers=N no-trigger=N no-signal=N` line, and exits 0 because it reports and does not gate |
135: | README structure | `python3 .skilled/skills/sk-doc/scripts/validate_document.py .skilled/skills/sk-code/sk-code-quality/README.md --type readme` reports zero issues |
136: | Final claim | Hand to the surface verification workflow (`workflow-verify.md`). This mode does not make done or works claims |
137: 
138: ---
139: 
140: ## 7. RELATED DOCUMENTS
141: 
142: | Document | Purpose |
143: |---|---|
144: | [`SKILL.md`](./SKILL.md) | Runtime contract for the quality mode |
145: | [`ROUTER.md`](./ROUTER.md) | Machine router: intent map, resource map and routing pseudocode |

43: The mode's headline strength is routing by target path: every surface family lands on the checklist that covers it, so the gate checks the same things a human reviewer would check. The universal floor applies to every file. The rows below are this hub's own SKILLED surface, which loads for files the surface detection places in it.
44: 
45: | Target family | What the mode knows how to check |
46: |---|---|
47: | **OpenCode skills** | loads the skill-authoring checklist by target path |
48: | **OpenCode agents and commands** | routes to the agent-authoring and command-authoring checklists |
49: | **Spec folders** | routes to the spec-folder authoring checklist that `system-spec-kit` owns |
50: | **MCP servers** | routes to the MCP-server-authoring checklist |
51: | **Language files and config** | applies the language-specific and config checklists |
52: | **Your own surface** | a surface another skill declares, or a checklist your `.skilled/skills/sk-code/sk-code-quality/repository/quality.json` names, brings its own checklists |
53: 
54: ---
55: 
56: ## 3. QUICK START
57: 
58: **Step 1: Route after implementation.** Use this mode after the surface skill (`sk-code-skilled`) has changed files and before the surface verification workflow (`workflow-verify.md`) collects final evidence.
59: 
60: **Step 2: Run the quality runner.**
61: 
62: ```bash
63: node .skilled/skills/sk-code/sk-code-quality/scripts/quality-gate.cjs --format text
64: ```
65: 
66: The runner reads the change, by default the working tree against `HEAD`. It runs the conflict-marker, secret and debug-leftover sensors, one comment-hygiene call over the changed files and a parse floor, and probes which hooks and workflows enforce hygiene. It prints one verdict with a gate and an exit code from 0 to 4. No gate means pass: exit 0 says only that no blocker was found and that every required check produced evidence. [`references/runner-contract.md`](./references/runner-contract.md) documents every field. A committed `.skilled/skills/sk-code/sk-code-quality/repository/quality.json` runs its commands only in a trusted repository. Without a grant each configured check reads `SKIPPED_UNTRUSTED` with the repair `git config --local skilled.trustRepoChecks true`, and [section 8 of the quality config reference](./references/quality-config.md) names the grants.
67: 
68: **Step 3: Load the checklists the verdict names.** The universal floor [`code-quality-standards.md`](../shared/references/universal/code-quality-standards.md) loads for every target. It gives each rule an id and marks it FIXED or overridable. [`universal-checklist.md`](../sk-code-skilled/assets/checklists/universal-checklist.md) is the SKILLED house checklist, and it loads only when SKILLED is a resolved surface. On SKILLED it also names the JavaScript and CSS house checks for a `.js` or `.css` target, in [`js-css-style/`](../sk-code-skilled/assets/checklists/js-css-style/). For `.skilled/` targets it names the matching checklist under [`../sk-code-skilled/assets/checklists/`](../sk-code-skilled/assets/checklists/). The house style of this framework (file layout, `MODULE:` headers, the `ceiling:` marker, test layout) lives in those SKILLED files, so another repository does not inherit it.
69: 
70: **Step 4: Fix or hand back.** Fix in-place quality failures with `Edit`. Root-cause failures that need investigation to the surface debugging workflow (`workflow-debug.md`). Send final evidence to the surface verification workflow (`workflow-verify.md`).
71: 
72: ---
73: 
74: ## 4. HOW IT WORKS
75: 
76: The mode sits between implementation and verification. It runs the quality runner over the changed files, which resolves surface identity through the shared surface reader and names the checklists that apply. The mode loads them and checks P0/P1/P2 status. P0 blocks completion. P1 is fixed unless the user accepts a documented risk. P2 is fixed when cheap or explicitly deferred with a reason.
77: 
78: ### The P0/P1/P2 Gate
79: 
80: | Severity | Meaning | Gate effect |
81: |---|---|---|
82: | **P0** | Correctness, safety, broken contract, forbidden comment metadata, unchecked generated drift or missing checklist evidence | Blocks completion until fixed or escalated |
83: | **P1** | Maintainability or authoring-contract issue that would confuse future work | Fixed before handoff unless the user accepts a documented risk |
84: | **P2** | Local polish or minor consistency issue with low behavioral risk | Fixed when cheap, otherwise deferred with a documented reason |
85: 
86: ### Target-Path Routing
87: 
88: OpenCode authoring targets route to specific checklists: skills, agents, commands, MCP servers, language files and config each have their own checklist under `sk-code-skilled`. Spec folders route to the spec-folder authoring checklist that `system-spec-kit` owns. `node scripts/quality-gate.cjs --explain <path> [<path>...]` answers for a whole change in one call. For each file it names the surfaces, the folder each surface loads from and every checklist with the seat that declared it, plus each checklist's parsed `## Rule overrides` rows. It runs nothing and writes nothing. It exits 2 when every path resolves, and 3 (ERROR) on a usage error or a missing path.
89: 
90: ### Rules Your Repository Can Change
91: 
92: The universal floor splits into FIXED rules and overridable ones. The hard floor stays on in every repository: secrets, conflict markers, parse failures, input validation, silent failures, initialization safety, resource cleanup and accessibility for UI code. A repository can drop or replace the rest, such as documentation, typing strictness, naming and the `ceiling:` marker.
93: 
94: There are two ways to say so, and they work together.
95: 
96: - **A `## Rule overrides` section** in a checklist the repository already declares, such as one named in `.skilled/skills/sk-code/sk-code-quality/repository/quality.json` `checklists[]`. Each row gives a rule id, `none` or `replace: <text>` and an optional reason. The shared contract is [`rule-overrides.md`](../shared/references/universal/rule-overrides.md), and `node ../shared/scripts/check-rule-overrides.cjs <checklist.md>` checks a section. A row that names a hard-floor id is refused.
97: - **`commentHygiene.disableRules`** in `.skilled/skills/sk-code/sk-code-quality/repository/quality.json` switches off named core comment-hygiene rules, such as `issue` or `task`. The runner, the pre-commit hook and the CI job all honor it, and the verdict lists what is off in `config.hygiene.disabled`. An unknown id, or a hard-floor id such as `secret.private-key`, is `CONFIG_INVALID`.
98: 
99: A run reads the section of every checklist it loads. A refused section, or a row whose rule id no declaring document carries, ends the run `ERROR` with `CONFIG_INVALID` and exit 3, and the error names the checklist and every reason. Each accepted row is recorded in `rule_overrides` and in the envelope's `p0_p1_p2_decisions` as `override <rule id> <none|replace> from <checklist>`, ahead of `PENDING_AGENT_JUDGMENT`. Two checklists at one precedence level that disagree on a rule leave its default in force, appear in `rule_conflicts` and join `summary.unverified`, so the gate reads `UNVERIFIED`.
100: 
101: A recorded hygiene row tells the agent and the review mode what to apply. The runner's own comment-hygiene check changes only through `disableRules`, so a repository that wants a hygiene rule off everywhere sets both. `--explain` shows what each checklist's section says and the conflicts for each file, and `/doctor:sk-code quality` shows the same answer for the whole repository.
102: 
103: ### The Mutation Boundary
104: 
105: This mode can edit already-scoped files because author-side quality correction is part of implementation. It cannot write new files and cannot dispatch subagents. Findings-only review belongs to `sk-code-review`.
106: 
107: ---
108: 
109: ## 5. INTEGRATION & NAVIGATION
110: 
111: ### When To Use This Mode
112: 
113: Use it when a change is already written and needs standards enforcement before final verification: skill authoring, script changes, config changes, frontend quality, comment hygiene or stale generated-output checks. Skip it when the task is to build new behavior, debug a failing symptom, verify non-mutating evidence or review without editing.
114:

118: |---|---|

120: | `sk-code-skilled` | Surface skills that implement and change files, own root-cause debugging and gather verification evidence through the implement → debug → verify workflow doctrine |
121: | `sk-code-review` | Produces findings-first reports when no author-side editing is wanted |
122: 
123: ---
124:

126: 
127: | Check | How to run it |
128: |---|---|
129: | Quality verdict | `node .skilled/skills/sk-code/sk-code-quality/scripts/quality-gate.cjs` prints one `code-quality-run/v1` verdict and exits 0 to 4, as `references/runner-contract.md` section 2 states. It writes no file |

153: ## 4. HOW IT WORKS
154: 
155: ### Quality Gate Workflow
156: 
157: 1. Resolve the surface and lifecycle state through the shared router. If no implementation changed files yet, route to the appropriate surface skill (`sk-code-skilled`) unless the user explicitly asked for a standalone quality audit.
158: 2. Collect the changed-file set from the task context or targeted paths. Read each target before editing.
159: 3. Run `node scripts/quality-gate.cjs` from the repository root. It takes the working-tree change by default, or `--base <ref>` or `--files <path>...`. Read the gate before anything else.
160:    `BLOCKED` means fix in place or escalate.
161:    `UNVERIFIED` means a required check produced no evidence or two override sources at one level disagree on a rule, so hand each check or rule id in `summary.unverified` to verification as an open claim.
162:    `NOTHING_CHECKED` is reported as such and never as clean. `ERROR` stops the gate until its `errors[]` entry is repaired.
163: 4. Load every checklist the verdict's `checklists[]` names, with the `why` it gives. The universal floor `../shared/references/universal/code-quality-standards.md` is always one of them.
164: 5. Judge each item in `judgment_required`. No built-in check decides input validation, silent failures, initialization safety, commented-out code, accessibility or design restraint.
165: 6. Apply the P0/P1/P2 model: P0 blocks completion, P1 should be fixed before handoff unless explicitly accepted, P2 can be documented when there is a clear reason.
166: 7. Before a gate fix adds code, apply the Design Restraint Ladder in `../shared/references/universal/code-quality-standards.md` and stop at the first rung that holds.
167: 8. Fix gate failures in place with `Edit` when the correction is limited to already-authored files, then rerun the runner.
168: 9. If a gate failure requires new files, broader implementation, or behavior design, hand back to the acting agent applying `workflow-implement.md`.
169: 10. If a gate failure is caused by an unclear runtime failure, hand to the surface's debugging workflow (`workflow-debug.md`) with the observed command, output, and failing target.
170: 11. When P0 items are clear, render `node scripts/quality-gate.cjs --format envelope`, fill its three `PENDING_AGENT_JUDGMENT` fields, and hand to the surface's verification workflow (`workflow-verify.md`) for non-mutating evidence before any done-claim.
171: 
172: ### P0/P1/P2 Author Checks
173: 
174: The tier rules and the P0 categories live in [`code-quality-standards.md`](../shared/references/universal/code-quality-standards.md): the tiers in its section 2, and the P0 categories with the mechanical floor in its section 3.
175: 
176: | Severity | Meaning | Gate Effect |
177: | --- | --- | --- |
178: | P0 | Correctness, safety, broken contract, or forbidden comment metadata | Blocks completion until fixed or escalated. |
179: | UNVERIFIED | Unchecked generated drift, missing required checklist evidence, a required check that produced no evidence, or two override sources at one level that disagree on a rule | Neither clean nor blocked. The claim stays open until verification proves it with its own command or reports it open. |
180: | P1 | Maintainability, routing, style, or authoring-contract issue likely to confuse future work | Fix before handoff unless the user accepts a documented risk. |
181: | P2 | Local polish, clarity, or minor consistency issue with low behavioral risk | Fix when cheap; otherwise document the deferral and why it is safe. |
182: 
183: ### Author-Side, Not Review-Side
184: 
185: Quality mode is allowed to edit because it is part of the implementation lifecycle. It should leave the workspace better than it found it, but only inside the current scope. If the requested output is a review report, use `sk-code-review`; if the requested output is evidence that commands pass, use the surface's verification workflow (`workflow-verify.md`).
186: 
187: ### Comment Hygiene
188: 
189: Comments should explain durable WHY and constraints. They must not embed temporary artifact labels, spec paths, packet labels, ticket labels, or phase bookkeeping. When this mode finds a violation, it edits the comment to preserve the durable reason or removes the comment if it has no durable value.
190: 
191: ### Advisory Evidence-Handoff Envelope
192: 
193: When the orchestrator or surface workflow requests structured evidence, append this advisory envelope after the prose handoff. Never place it in a position that reads as a status verdict, and never let it stand in for the handoff to the surface's verification workflow (`workflow-verify.md`).
194: 
195: ```text
196: CODE_QUALITY_RESULT v1
197: schema_version: code-quality/v1
198: status: advisory
199: modified_files: <repo-relative paths, or none>
200: resolved_surface: <declared surface label(s) in detection order | unknown>
201: checklists_loaded: <checklist paths loaded, or none>
202: checker_outputs: code-quality-run/v1 gate=<GATE> exit=<n> p0_blocking=<n> unverified=<ids|none> unchecked=<n> layers=pc:<state>,ci:<state>,pe:<state>
203: p0_p1_p2_decisions: <per-severity dispositions>
204: accepted_deferrals: <documented P1/P2 deferrals and why safe, or none>
205: verification_handoff: workflow-verify.md
206: remaining_accepted_risk: <one-line residual risk, or none>
207: ```
208: 
209: `node scripts/quality-gate.cjs --format envelope` renders the machine fields, and `references/runner-contract.md` section 4 holds the grammar.
210: The three judgment fields, `p0_p1_p2_decisions`, `accepted_deferrals` and `remaining_accepted_risk`, print as `PENDING_AGENT_JUDGMENT` until the agent fills them, and a field that still reads it is open work.
211: `p0_p1_p2_decisions` also lists each `## Rule overrides` row the run applied, as `override <rule id> <none|replace> from <checklist file>`, and each `override-conflict <rule id> <checklist file> <checklist file>` between two checklists at one precedence level, ahead of the marker.
212: A conflicting rule keeps its default and is unverified.
213: A refused override section, or one with a row whose id no rule carries, ends the run `CONFIG_INVALID`, exit 3.
214: A private surface prints by its label only, so the envelope never names a `local-` skill.
215: 
216: This envelope is advisory and additive only: its `status` is fixed to `advisory` and MUST NOT be `pass`, `success`, or `done`. Its presence NEVER reads as a completion, done, works, or passing claim, and it never replaces the handoff to the surface's verification workflow (`workflow-verify.md`) — it reinforces, and does not relax, the §5 NEVER rule that this mode makes no passing claims.

220: ## 5. RULES
221: 
222: ### ✅ ALWAYS
223: 
224: 1. Read target files before editing them.
225: 2. Run the runner, `node scripts/quality-gate.cjs`, before any implementation-done or quality-pass claim, and load every checklist its `checklists[]` names. The universal floor is always one of them.
226: 3. Resolve surface identity through `../shared/references/stack-detection.md`; do not re-author surface detection in this packet.
227: 4. Load the SKILLED authoring checklist the verdict names before checking `.skilled/` work, and the MCP server checklist by judgment for MCP server source.
228: 5. Let the runner call `scripts/check-comment-hygiene.sh` over every modified comment-capable file, or run the checker directly on one file outside a runner call.
229: 6. Fix P0 issues before handing to verification unless the only safe action is escalation.
230: 7. Keep fixes scoped to quality-gate failures in files already in scope.
231: 8. Hand failures that need root-cause investigation to the surface's debugging workflow (`workflow-debug.md`) with the exact symptom and evidence.
232: 
233: ### ⛔ NEVER
234: 
235: 1. Never create new files; this mode has no `Write` authority.
236: 2. Never dispatch subagents; this mode has no `Task` authority.
237: 3. Never make completion, done, works, or passing claims; hand to the surface's verification workflow (`workflow-verify.md`) for evidence.
238: 4. Never replace a formal findings-first review; route that to `sk-code-review`.
239: 5. Never paste or fork shared surface-detection, quality, or style references into this packet.
240: 6. Never broaden scope into cleanup or refactor work unrelated to the gate failure.
241: 7. Never allow ephemeral artifact labels in code comments; preserve durable WHY only.
242: 8. Never add a packet-local `graph-metadata.json`.
243: 9. Never run a command the repository layer does not name. The runner runs its built-in checks and the commands the repository's committed config names, and this mode adds no command of its own.
244: 10. Never read `NOTHING_CHECKED` or `UNVERIFIED` as clean. Each names evidence that does not exist yet.
245: 
246: ### ⚠️ ESCALATE IF
247: 
248: 1. A required P0 check is UNVERIFIED and only the operator can name or install its tool.
249: 2. The correct checklist cannot be identified from the target path.
250: 3. A P0 issue requires new files, new behavior, or scope beyond an in-place quality fix.
251: 4. Comment-hygiene enforcement layers disagree on a blocking result.
252: 5. Generated artifacts appear stale but the regeneration command is unknown or unsafe to run.

256: ## 6. SUCCESS CRITERIA
257: 
258: - The quality gate ran after implementation and before verification.
259: - Surface identity came from the shared router, not packet-local detection logic.
260: - `scripts/quality-gate.cjs` ran on the change, and its gate is quoted as printed, never restated as a pass.
261: - Every checklist the verdict's `checklists[]` names was loaded before any quality-pass claim, the universal floor among them.
262: - The comment-hygiene result came from the runner's single checker call, with zero blocking findings or a documented escalation.
263: - Each id in `summary.unverified` is handed to verification as an open claim.
264: - P0 issues are fixed in place or escalated with evidence; P1/P2 handling is explicit.
265: - No new files were authored by this mode.
266: - Handoff to the surface's verification workflow (`workflow-verify.md`) includes the quality evidence and any remaining accepted risk.

10: # Code Quality (quality)
11: 
12: `quality` is the author-side quality gate MODE child of the `sk-code` family.
13: It runs after the acting agent applying `workflow-implement.md` changes the code and before the surface's verification workflow or done-claim.
14: It consumes the shared surface router, loads the right checklist for the detected surface and target path, fixes quality-gate failures in place, and leaves findings-only output to `sk-code-review`.
15: 
16: ---
17: 
18: ## 1. WHEN TO USE
19: 
20: ### Activation Triggers
21: 
22: Use this mode when the request involves:
23: - Running the post-implementation quality gate before a completion claim.
24: - Applying P0/P1/P2 author-side checks to changed code, scripts, skills, agents, commands, MCP servers, or spec docs.
25: - Checking comment hygiene on modified files and removing ephemeral artifact references from comments while preserving durable WHY.
26: - Loading a SKILLED authoring checklist for `.skilled/skills/`, `.skilled/agents/`, `.skilled/commands/`, `specs/`, MCP server source, or language-specific SKILLED files.
27: - Fixing quality-gate failures in place with `Edit` when the fix belongs to the already-authored file.
28: 
29: Keyword triggers: `quality gate`, `code quality`, `comment hygiene`, `surface checklist`, `authoring checklist`, `SKILLED checklist`, `check before done`.
30: 
31: ### When NOT to Use
32: 
33: Skip this mode when:
34: - The user needs code written, files scaffolded, or behavior implemented. Hand it to the acting agent applying `workflow-implement.md` for the detected surface.
35: - A failure needs symptom-to-root-cause investigation or a single-cause bug fix. Use the surface's debugging workflow (`workflow-debug.md`).
36: - The task is to collect final non-mutating verification evidence. Use the surface's verification workflow (`workflow-verify.md`).
37: - The user asks for findings-first review output, severity-ranked findings, or PR review. Use `sk-code-review`.
38: - The task is documentation-only prose with no code-work contract. Use `sk-doc`.
39: 
40: ### Family Boundary
41: 
42: This is an independently invokable member of the `sk-code` family. It owns the quality gate, not implementation planning, debugging, verification evidence, or formal review reporting. It may edit files that the surface skill already changed to satisfy gate failures, but it does not create new files and does not dispatch subagents.
43: 
44: Pairs well with:
45: - The surface skill (`sk-code-skilled`) immediately before this gate, because implementation writes the files this mode checks.
46: - The surface's debugging workflow (`workflow-debug.md`) when a quality failure reveals a functional bug or failing command.
47: - The surface's verification workflow (`workflow-verify.md`) after P0 quality issues are clear, because verification gates the final claim.
48: - `sk-code-review` when the user wants findings-only output rather than author-side correction.
49: 
50: ---
51: 
52: ## 2. SMART ROUTING
53: 
54: The `sk-code` hub routes a post-implementation quality gate here: the request names a quality gate, comment hygiene, an authoring checklist or a check before done, and the hub's `quality` signal selects this packet.
55: This mode routes by target path more than by keyword, because the checklists a change needs follow the files it touches.
56: `node scripts/quality-gate.cjs --explain <path>` names those checklists and why, and its answer outranks any keyword match.
57: 
58: Three resources load first: `references/runner-contract.md` for the runner's CLI, gate values and verdict;
59: `../shared/references/universal/code-quality-standards.md` for the shared severity floor; and `references/code-style-guide.md` for this packet's style and comment rules.
60: The resource domains, loading levels, path-keyed rows and comment-hygiene layers follow in the next section.
61: 
62: The prompt-intent projection in that router only makes the default resources scoreable; it never picks the path-keyed checklist.
63: Read [`ROUTER.md`](./ROUTER.md) before selecting skill-local resources; open only the matched files.
64: 
65: ---
66: 
67: ## 3. RESOURCES
68: 
69: ### Resource Domains
70: 
71: - This mode ships no house-style checklist. The universal floor and the universal style guide apply on every surface, and each surface's own checklists carry its house style.
72:   `../sk-code-skilled/assets/checklists/universal-checklist.md` is the SKILLED baseline, loaded when SKILLED is a resolved surface of the target, and the SKILLED JavaScript and CSS house checks sit under `../sk-code-skilled/assets/checklists/js-css-style/`.
73: - `../sk-code-skilled/assets/checklists/` contains OpenCode authoring checklists for skills, agents, commands, MCP servers, language files, and config; the spec-folder checklist is owned by `system-spec-kit`.
74: - `scripts/quality-gate.cjs` is the runner. It reads the change, runs the built-in checks, probes the enforcement layers, lists the checklists the declarations name and prints one verdict. It writes no file.
75:   The only commands it runs beyond its own are the ones a repository's committed `.skilled/skills/sk-code/sk-code-quality/repository/quality.json` names, each as an argv array under a deadline and the workspace guard, and only once the repository is trusted (`references/quality-config.md` section 8).
76:   A command a manifest implies is reported as a suggestion it never runs.
77:   `references/runner-contract.md` holds its CLI, gate values, verdict, envelope grammar and rule ids, and `references/quality-config.md` holds the repository config: its schema, discovery order, merge rule and trust boundary.
78: - `assets/quality-defaults.json` holds the runner's base layer: excluded paths, sensor settings and the checklist rows this mode owns. It names no command.
79: - `scripts/check-comment-hygiene.sh` is the per-file comment-hygiene gate. The runner calls it once per run with `--json`.
80: - `scripts/check-dist-staleness.sh` checks generated/distribution artifact drift when that is part of the target.
81: - `scripts/ceiling-report.sh [<file>...]` lists the `ceiling:` and `intentional-limit:` comment markers and tags the ones with no trigger or no measurable signal.
82:   Run it for a debt pass, before a release or when a reviewer asks what limits the code knowingly accepts.
83:   It reads every tracked code file, or only the files named, prints one `path:line  text  [tags]` line per marker and a closing `markers=N no-trigger=N no-signal=N` line, and exits 0 because it reports and does not gate.
84: - `scripts/hooks/claude-posttooluse.sh` is the legacy write-time hook, kept for direct tests and registered in no runtime. The live write-time warning is `.skilled/hooks/post-edit-quality/claude/claude-posttooluse.cjs`.
85: - `../shared/references/universal/code-quality-standards.md` is the cross-mode severity standard this packet consumes, and `references/code-style-guide.md` is this packet's own style and comment-hygiene guide.
86: 
87: ### Resource Loading Levels
88: 
89: | Level | When to Load | Resources |
90: | --- | --- | --- |
91: | ALWAYS | Any quality-gate invocation | `../shared/references/stack-detection.md`, `../ROUTER.md`, `../shared/references/phase-detection.md` |
92: | ALWAYS | Before any implementation-done claim | `references/runner-contract.md`, `../shared/references/universal/code-quality-standards.md`, `references/code-style-guide.md` |
93: | ALWAYS | Any quality-gate invocation on changed files | `scripts/quality-gate.cjs`, which calls `scripts/check-comment-hygiene.sh` once over every modified file |
94: | CONDITIONAL | The verdict lists a checklist | Every file in the runner's `checklists[]`, each with the `why` the verdict gives |
95: | CONDITIONAL | The repository has or needs `.skilled/skills/sk-code/sk-code-quality/repository/quality.json`, or the verdict reports a configured check, a config error or a suggestion | `references/quality-config.md` |
96: | CONDITIONAL | SKILLED is a resolved surface of the target | `../sk-code-skilled/assets/checklists/universal-checklist.md` |
97: | CONDITIONAL | A direct check on one file, outside a runner call | `scripts/check-comment-hygiene.sh` |
98: | CONDITIONAL | `.skilled/skills/` target | `../sk-code-skilled/assets/checklists/skill-authoring.md` |
99: | CONDITIONAL | `.skilled/agents/` target | `../sk-code-skilled/assets/checklists/agent-authoring.md` |

102: | CONDITIONAL | MCP server source | `../sk-code-skilled/assets/checklists/mcp-server-authoring.md` |
103: | CONDITIONAL | OpenCode JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, Shell, Rust, JSON, or JSONC files | `../sk-code-skilled/assets/checklists/javascript-checklist.md`, `../sk-code-skilled/assets/checklists/typescript-checklist.md`, `../sk-code-skilled/assets/checklists/python-checklist.md`, `../sk-code-skilled/assets/checklists/shell-checklist.md`, `../sk-code-skilled/assets/checklists/rust-checklist/overview-and-p0-parity.md`, `../sk-code-skilled/assets/checklists/rust-checklist/p0-safety-and-boundary-discipline.md`, `../sk-code-skilled/assets/checklists/rust-checklist/p1-required.md`, `../sk-code-skilled/assets/checklists/rust-checklist/p2-evidence-validation-and-resources.md`, `../sk-code-skilled/assets/checklists/config-checklist.md` as applicable |

105: | ON_DEMAND | Debt pass, before a release or a reviewer asks what limits the code knowingly accepts | `scripts/ceiling-report.sh` |
106: | ON_DEMAND | Need the legacy write-time hook's behavior, which no runtime registers | `scripts/hooks/claude-posttooluse.sh` |
107: 
108: ### Target-Path Checklist Map
109: 
110: The runner resolves checklists from two sources: the rows this mode owns in `assets/quality-defaults.json`, which are the universal floor and, in this hub's own repository, the spec-folder authoring checklist, and each surface's `quality.checklists` declaration.
111: Ask the runner which checklists apply to a file, and why, with `node scripts/quality-gate.cjs --explain <path>`. Its `checklists[]` and each entry's `why` are the answer, in any repository.
112: This repository's own map, the SKILLED rows among them, is rendered in `../sk-code-skilled/SKILL.md` under "Quality Checklist Map".
113: `/doctor:sk-code quality` shows the same answer for a whole repository: every checklist the gate would load, its seat, its override rows and the hygiene rules that apply.
114: 
115: **A repository outside this hub declares its rules in its own config.** The runner reads surface declarations only from the hub that holds it: the hub's `mode-registry.json` and the `graph-metadata.json` of each skill in the skills folder beside that hub.
116: A surface skill that lives in the repository under test, or in any other checkout, is never discovered, even when it declares `surface_detection` and a `quality` block.
117: Such a repository names its rules in `.skilled/skills/sk-code/sk-code-quality/repository/quality.json` instead.
118: Each `checklists[]` row names a repository-relative checklist file and selects files by `paths`, `extensions` or `contentMarkers`.
119: A file the row names may carry a `## Rule overrides` section, read through the shared linter `../shared/scripts/check-rule-overrides.cjs`, to drop or replace a rule outside the hard floor at the repository level, which ranks above every surface.
120: The limit stays: such a row adds a checklist and never a surface label, so `--explain` lists the checklist while its `surfaces` and `surface_skills` never name a surface of the repository's own.
121: `references/quality-config.md` section 3 holds the row rules.
122: 
123: ### Comment-Hygiene Enforcement Gates
124: 
125: This mode owns the author-side check and knows the three independent enforcement layers. In any repository, the runner's `layers` field reports what a probe found for each one, `present`, `absent`, `untrusted`, `broken` or `unknown`, and a quality claim cites that field, never this table.
126: 
127: **This repository's wiring.** The table and the notes after it describe this hub's own repository. They are not universal: another repository may wire none of these layers, or wire them differently.
128: 
129: | Gate | Where | Effect |
130: | --- | --- | --- |
131: | Write-time warning | `.skilled/hooks/post-edit-quality/claude/claude-posttooluse.cjs`, wired as the Claude `PostToolUse` hook for `Write` and `Edit` in `.claude/settings.json` | Warns during authoring when a comment carries ephemeral artifact labels. |
132: | Pre-commit block | `.skilled/scripts/git-hooks/pre-commit`, installed through `core.hooksPath` by `.skilled/scripts/install-git-hooks.sh` | Blocks commits with forbidden comment patterns across runtimes. |
133: | CI block | `.github/workflows/comment-hygiene.yml` | Blocks pull requests with forbidden comment patterns. |
134: 
135: A repository can switch named core hygiene rules off with `commentHygiene.disableRules` in its quality config, never a rule the shared `rule-overrides.json` fixes.
136: The runner, the pre-commit block and the CI block all read that key through `scripts/lib/quality-config.cjs`, so a rule switched off for one is off for all three.
137: The config's additions, such as a ticket prefix, reach the runner alone, so the pre-commit and CI blocks keep the core set minus the disabled rules, and `config.hygiene.disabled` in the verdict names what is off.
138: The write-time warning still applies every core rule, and it never blocks.
139: `references/quality-config.md` holds the key's rules.
140: 
141: The write-time warning is one adapter of the shared router in `.skilled/hooks/post-edit-quality/`, which runs after every edit through one adapter per runtime (Claude Code, Codex, Devin, Cursor, Pi and OpenCode) and reports findings before the model's next turn.
142: The pre-commit block can be bypassed for one commit with `SPECKIT_SKIP_COMMENT_HYGIENE=1 git commit`, and the CI block re-checks every PR to main, which `--no-verify` cannot skip.
143: The live `.skilled/scripts/git-hooks/pre-commit` also runs the agent-mirror-sync gate and other repository gates, independent of comment hygiene, documented in `.skilled/scripts/git-hooks/README.md`.
144: The older `.skilled/hooks/git/pre-commit` and `scripts/hooks/claude-posttooluse.sh` are compatibility helpers kept for direct tests. Neither is an installed hook.
145: 
146: Run `node scripts/quality-gate.cjs`, which calls `scripts/check-comment-hygiene.sh` once over every modified file that can contain comments.
147: A finding on a changed line blocks.
148: A finding on an unchanged line of a touched file blocks only when `layers` reports the pre-commit or CI layer `present`, because that layer scans whole files and would fail the change anyway.
149: Otherwise it is P1 touched-file debt the change did not write.
150: 
151: ---
152: 
153: ## 4. HOW IT WORKS
154: 
155: ### Quality Gate Workflow
156: 
157: 1. Resolve the surface and lifecycle state through the shared router. If no implementation changed files yet, route to the appropriate surface skill (`sk-code-skilled`) unless the user explicitly asked for a standalone quality audit.
158: 2. Collect the changed-file set from the task context or targeted paths. Read each target before editing.
159: 3. Run `node scripts/quality-gate.cjs` from the repository root. It takes the working-tree change by default, or `--base <ref>` or `--files <path>...`. Read the gate before anything else.
160:    `BLOCKED` means fix in place or escalate.
161:    `UNVERIFIED` means a required check produced no evidence or two override sources at one level disagree on a rule, so hand each check or rule id in `summary.unverified` to verification as an open claim.
162:    `NOTHING_CHECKED` is reported as such and never as clean. `ERROR` stops the gate until its `errors[]` entry is repaired.
163: 4. Load every checklist the verdict's `checklists[]` names, with the `why` it gives. The universal floor `../shared/references/universal/code-quality-standards.md` is always one of them.
164: 5. Judge each item in `judgment_required`. No built-in check decides input validation, silent failures, initialization safety, commented-out code, accessibility or design restraint.
165: 6. Apply the P0/P1/P2 model: P0 blocks completion, P1 should be fixed before handoff unless explicitly accepted, P2 can be documented when there is a clear reason.
166: 7. Before a gate fix adds code, apply the Design Restraint Ladder in `../shared/references/universal/code-quality-standards.md` and stop at the first rung that holds.
167: 8. Fix gate failures in place with `Edit` when the correction is limited to already-authored files, then rerun the runner.
168: 9. If a gate failure requires new files, broader implementation, or behavior design, hand back to the acting agent applying `workflow-implement.md`.
169: 10. If a gate failure is caused by an unclear runtime failure, hand to the surface's debugging workflow (`workflow-debug.md`) with the observed command, output, and failing target.
170: 11. When P0 items are clear, render `node scripts/quality-gate.cjs --format envelope`, fill its three `PENDING_AGENT_JUDGMENT` fields, and hand to the surface's verification workflow (`workflow-verify.md`) for non-mutating evidence before any done-claim.
171: 
172: ### P0/P1/P2 Author Checks
173: 
174: The tier rules and the P0 categories live in [`code-quality-standards.md`](../shared/references/universal/code-quality-standards.md): the tiers in its section 2, and the P0 categories with the mechanical floor in its section 3.
175: 
176: | Severity | Meaning | Gate Effect |
177: | --- | --- | --- |
178: | P0 | Correctness, safety, broken contract, or forbidden comment metadata | Blocks completion until fixed or escalated. |
179: | UNVERIFIED | Unchecked generated drift, missing required checklist evidence, a required check that produced no evidence, or two override sources at one level that disagree on a rule | Neither clean nor blocked. The claim stays open until verification proves it with its own command or reports it open. |
180: | P1 | Maintainability, routing, style, or authoring-contract issue likely to confuse future work | Fix before handoff unless the user accepts a documented risk. |
181: | P2 | Local polish, clarity, or minor consistency issue with low behavioral risk | Fix when cheap; otherwise document the deferral and why it is safe. |
182: 
183: ### Author-Side, Not Review-Side
184: 
185: Quality mode is allowed to edit because it is part of the implementation lifecycle. It should leave the workspace better than it found it, but only inside the current scope. If the requested output is a review report, use `sk-code-review`; if the requested output is evidence that commands pass, use the surface's verification workflow (`workflow-verify.md`).
186: 
187: ### Comment Hygiene
188: 
189: Comments should explain durable WHY and constraints. They must not embed temporary artifact labels, spec paths, packet labels, ticket labels, or phase bookkeeping. When this mode finds a violation, it edits the comment to preserve the durable reason or removes the comment if it has no durable value.
190: 
191: ### Advisory Evidence-Handoff Envelope
192: 
193: When the orchestrator or surface workflow requests structured evidence, append this advisory envelope after the prose handoff. Never place it in a position that reads as a status verdict, and never let it stand in for the handoff to the surface's verification workflow (`workflow-verify.md`).
194: 
195: ```text
196: CODE_QUALITY_RESULT v1
197: schema_version: code-quality/v1
198: status: advisory
199: modified_files: <repo-relative paths, or none>
200: resolved_surface: <declared surface label(s) in detection order | unknown>
201: checklists_loaded: <checklist paths loaded, or none>
202: checker_outputs: code-quality-run/v1 gate=<GATE> exit=<n> p0_blocking=<n> unverified=<ids|none> unchecked=<n> layers=pc:<state>,ci:<state>,pe:<state>
203: p0_p1_p2_decisions: <per-severity dispositions>
204: accepted_deferrals: <documented P1/P2 deferrals and why safe, or none>
205: verification_handoff: workflow-verify.md
206: remaining_accepted_risk: <one-line residual risk, or none>
207: ```
208: 
209: `node scripts/quality-gate.cjs --format envelope` renders the machine fields, and `references/runner-contract.md` section 4 holds the grammar.
210: The three judgment fields, `p0_p1_p2_decisions`, `accepted_deferrals` and `remaining_accepted_risk`, print as `PENDING_AGENT_JUDGMENT` until the agent fills them, and a field that still reads it is open work.
211: `p0_p1_p2_decisions` also lists each `## Rule overrides` row the run applied, as `override <rule id> <none|replace> from <checklist file>`, and each `override-conflict <rule id> <checklist file> <checklist file>` between two checklists at one precedence level, ahead of the marker.
212: A conflicting rule keeps its default and is unverified.
213: A refused override section, or one with a row whose id no rule carries, ends the run `CONFIG_INVALID`, exit 3.
214: A private surface prints by its label only, so the envelope never names a `local-` skill.
215: 
216: This envelope is advisory and additive only: its `status` is fixed to `advisory` and MUST NOT be `pass`, `success`, or `done`. Its presence NEVER reads as a completion, done, works, or passing claim, and it never replaces the handoff to the surface's verification workflow (`workflow-verify.md`) — it reinforces, and does not relax, the §5 NEVER rule that this mode makes no passing claims.
217: 
218: ---
219: 
220: ## 5. RULES
221: 
222: ### ✅ ALWAYS
223: 
224: 1. Read target files before editing them.
225: 2. Run the runner, `node scripts/quality-gate.cjs`, before any implementation-done or quality-pass claim, and load every checklist its `checklists[]` names. The universal floor is always one of them.
226: 3. Resolve surface identity through `../shared/references/stack-detection.md`; do not re-author surface detection in this packet.
227: 4. Load the SKILLED authoring checklist the verdict names before checking `.skilled/` work, and the MCP server checklist by judgment for MCP server source.
228: 5. Let the runner call `scripts/check-comment-hygiene.sh` over every modified comment-capable file, or run the checker directly on one file outside a runner call.
229: 6. Fix P0 issues before handing to verification unless the only safe action is escalation.
230: 7. Keep fixes scoped to quality-gate failures in files already in scope.
231: 8. Hand failures that need root-cause investigation to the surface's debugging workflow (`workflow-debug.md`) with the exact symptom and evidence.
232: 
233: ### ⛔ NEVER
234: 
235: 1. Never create new files; this mode has no `Write` authority.
236: 2. Never dispatch subagents; this mode has no `Task` authority.
237: 3. Never make completion, done, works, or passing claims; hand to the surface's verification workflow (`workflow-verify.md`) for evidence.
238: 4. Never replace a formal findings-first review; route that to `sk-code-review`.
239: 5. Never paste or fork shared surface-detection, quality, or style references into this packet.
240: 6. Never broaden scope into cleanup or refactor work unrelated to the gate failure.
241: 7. Never allow ephemeral artifact labels in code comments; preserve durable WHY only.
242: 8. Never add a packet-local `graph-metadata.json`.
243: 9. Never run a command the repository layer does not name. The runner runs its built-in checks and the commands the repository's committed config names, and this mode adds no command of its own.
244: 10. Never read `NOTHING_CHECKED` or `UNVERIFIED` as clean. Each names evidence that does not exist yet.
245: 
246: ### ⚠️ ESCALATE IF
247: 
248: 1. A required P0 check is UNVERIFIED and only the operator can name or install its tool.
249: 2. The correct checklist cannot be identified from the target path.
250: 3. A P0 issue requires new files, new behavior, or scope beyond an in-place quality fix.
251: 4. Comment-hygiene enforcement layers disagree on a blocking result.
252: 5. Generated artifacts appear stale but the regeneration command is unknown or unsafe to run.
253: 
254: ---
255: 
256: ## 6. SUCCESS CRITERIA
257: 
258: - The quality gate ran after implementation and before verification.
259: - Surface identity came from the shared router, not packet-local detection logic.
260: - `scripts/quality-gate.cjs` ran on the change, and its gate is quoted as printed, never restated as a pass.
261: - Every checklist the verdict's `checklists[]` names was loaded before any quality-pass claim, the universal floor among them.
262: - The comment-hygiene result came from the runner's single checker call, with zero blocking findings or a documented escalation.
263: - Each id in `summary.unverified` is handed to verification as an open claim.
264: - P0 issues are fixed in place or escalated with evidence; P1/P2 handling is explicit.
265: - No new files were authored by this mode.
266: - Handoff to the surface's verification workflow (`workflow-verify.md`) includes the quality evidence and any remaining accepted risk.
267: 
268: ---
269: 
270: ## 7. INTEGRATION POINTS
271: 
272: - `sk-code` routes quality prompts here through `mode-registry.json` and keeps the hub routing-only.
273: - The acting agent applying `workflow-implement.md` changes files before this gate runs, then applies the surface's `workflow-debug.md` and `workflow-verify.md`, which `sk-code-skilled` bundles as read-only doctrine.
274: - `sk-code-review` owns findings-first review output and PR-style severity reporting.
275: - `system-spec-kit` owns spec-folder documentation, validation, and memory workflows when the broader task requires them.
276: 
277: ---

14: # README Template and Selection Guide
15: 
16: Use this template for project, skill, feature and component READMEs. Use [`readme-code-template.md`](./readme-code-template.md) for source-folder READMEs that explain package topology, files, boundaries and data or control flow.
17: 
18: ---
19: 
20: ## 1. README SELECTION
21: 
22: README files answer two questions: what is this, and how does someone use or navigate it?
23: 
24: | Type | Use When | Template |
25: |---|---|---|
26: | Project | The repository or package needs a public entry point | This file |
27: | Skill | A skill needs human-facing context beyond `SKILL.md` | This file |
28: | Feature | A user-facing feature needs setup, usage or behavior notes | This file |
29: | Component | A reusable module has an API, examples or configuration | This file, trimmed |
30: | Code Folder | A source directory needs developer orientation | [`readme-code-template.md`](./readme-code-template.md) |
31: 
32: Create a README when someone can land in the folder and need orientation. Skip it when inline comments or a nearby parent README already explain the folder.
33: 
34: ```text
35: Is this a project, package, skill or feature root?
36: +-- Yes: write a general README.
37: `-- No: is this source-code orientation?
38:     +-- Yes: use readme_code_template.md.
39:     `-- No: write a focused README only if readers need setup, usage or navigation help.
40: ```
41: 
42: Keep READMEs current-state only. Do not cite spec packet numbers, phase IDs or migration history. Use feature names, file paths, commands and stable source links.
43: 
44: ---
45: 
46: ## 2. GENERAL STRUCTURE
47: 
48: Use only the sections that fit the audience. Project and skill READMEs often need most sections. Feature and component READMEs should stay shorter.
49: 
50: | Section | Include When | Content |
51: |---|---|---|
52: | Overview | Always | Purpose, audience, main value and prerequisites |
53: | Key Statistics | Useful facts help readers decide scope | Counts, version, supported modes, limits |
54: | How This Compares | Readers may confuse this with nearby tools | Short comparison table |
55: | Quick Start | Readers need to run or try something | Short setup, verification and first use |
56: | Features | Capabilities need explanation | Feature groups, behavior notes and examples |
57: | Requirements | Runtime, tool or service needs exist | Minimum versions, permissions and external services |
58: | Structure | Navigation matters | Directory tree and key files |
59: | Configuration | Settings exist | Config files, options, defaults and env vars |
60: | Usage Examples | Patterns are easier shown than described | Simple and advanced examples with expected results |
61: | Troubleshooting | Users can hit known issues | What they see, cause and fix |
62: | FAQ | Repeated questions exist | Short answers only |
63: | Related Resources | Always when links exist | Grouped skills, documents, commands or external references |
64: 
65: Code-folder READMEs are different. Do not force Quick Start, Features, FAQ or Troubleshooting unless the directory has runnable commands or known reader problems. Use [`readme-code-template.md`](./readme-code-template.md).
66: 
67: ---
68: 
69: ## 3. SKILL AND PROJECT PROFILE
70: 
71: Use this profile for OpenCode skills, package roots and project-level READMEs that need more than a bare overview.
72: 
73: | Profile Block | Good For | Keep It Short By |
74: |---|---|---|
75: | `trigger_phrases` | Search, memory and skill routing | 3-8 concrete phrases |
76: | Key Statistics | Skill counts, tool counts, version facts | Use one compact table |
77: | How This Compares | Neighboring skills or tools | Compare only reader-relevant differences |
78: | Key Features | Current capability inventory | Group related features |
79: | Requirements | Tooling and runtime needs | Separate required from optional |
80: | Related Skills | Skill graph navigation | Group by relationship type |
81: | Related Documents | Operator or developer references | Link stable docs, not packet history |
82: | FAQ | Repeated questions | 3-6 high-value Q&A pairs |
83: 
84: Sections use plain numbered H2 headings. Do not add `<!-- ANCHOR -->` comments or a Table of Contents.
85: 
86: ```markdown
87: ## 1. OVERVIEW
88: 
89: [Section content]
90: 
91: ```
92: 
93: ---
94: 
95: ## 4. WRITING RULES
96: 
97: Write for scanning first.
98: 
99: - Lead with what the thing does.
100: - Put the fastest useful path before detailed reference.
101: - Use tables for options, file lists and comparisons.
102: - Give every inventory item a description. When an item needs more than one line, switch to the itemized pattern below instead of widening the table.
103: - Use fenced code blocks with language tags.
104: - Test commands before documenting them.
105: - Show expected output for verification commands.
106: - Use relative links for local docs.
107: - Remove unused sections instead of leaving placeholders.
108: 
109: The itemized pattern for inventories where each item needs more than one line:
110: 
111: ```markdown
112: **`spec.md`**
113: - What the feature is and why it exists.
114: - Required at every level.
115: ```
116: 
117: Group related items under an unnumbered `#####` heading when the inventory has natural groups, for example by how each item is triggered.
118: 
119: Voice by README type:
120: 
121: | Type | Voice |
122: |---|---|
123: | Project, Skill, Feature | Plain explanation first, reference detail later |
124: | Component | Technical and concise |
125: | Code Folder | Technical and concise, via `readme-code-template.md` |
126: 
127: Human Voice Rules apply to all README content:
128: 
129: - No em dashes. Use commas, periods or colons.
130: - No semicolons. Split the sentence or use "and".
131: - No Oxford comma in inline lists.
132: - No setup phrases.
133: - No banned words from the HVR reference.
134: - Prefer active voice and direct verbs.
135: 
136: Full reference: [`hvr-rules.md`](../../sk-create-with-human-voice/references/hvr-rules.md).
137: 
138: ---
139: 
140: ## 5. FRONTMATTER
141: 
142: Frontmatter is optional for normal project READMEs and recommended for skill or system documentation that should be discoverable.
143: 
144: ```yaml
145: ---
146: title: "[DOCUMENT_TITLE]"
147: description: "[One-sentence description]"
148: trigger_phrases:
149:   - "[search phrase]"
150:   - "[routing phrase]"
151: ---
152: ```
153: 
154: Use frontmatter when it improves routing, search or maintenance. Omit it for small human-only documents.
155: 
156: ---
157: 
158: ## 6. FILLABLE SCAFFOLD
159: 
160: Copy this scaffold, then remove sections that do not apply.
161: 
162: ````markdown
163: ---
164: title: "[PROJECT_OR_FEATURE_NAME]"
165: description: "[One-sentence description]"
166: trigger_phrases:
167:   - "[search phrase]"
168: version: 1.0.0.0
169: ---
170: 
171: # [PROJECT_OR_FEATURE_NAME]
172: 
173: > [One-sentence purpose statement.]
174: 
175: ---
176: 
177: ## 1. OVERVIEW
178: 
179: [Explain what this is, who it is for and why it exists.]
180: 
181: ### Key Statistics
182: 
183: | Metric | Value |
184: |---|---|
185: | Status | [Current state] |
186: | Version | [Version or release channel] |
187: | Main audience | [Who uses this] |
188: | Operating modes | [Mode count or short list] |
189: 
190: ### How This Compares
191: 
192: | Capability | This Project | Related Option |
193: |---|---|---|
194: | [Capability] | [Current behavior] | [Difference] |
195: 
196: 
197: ---
198: 
199: ## 2. QUICK START
200: 
201: ```bash
202: # Install or prepare
203: [command]
204: 
205: # Verify
206: [command]
207: ```
208: 
209: Expected result: [what success looks like].
210: 
211: 
212: ---
213: 
214: ## 3. FEATURES
215: 
216: ### Key Features
217: 
218: | Feature | What It Does |
219: |---|---|
220: | [Feature] | [Current behavior] |
221: 
222: 
223: ---
224: 
225: ## 4. REQUIREMENTS
226: 
227: | Requirement | Minimum | Notes |
228: |---|---|---|
229: | [Runtime or tool] | [Version] | [Why it is needed] |
230: 
231: 
232: ---
233: 
234: ## 5. STRUCTURE
235: 
236: ```text
237: [root]/
238: +-- [path]/        # [Purpose]
239: `-- [file]         # [Purpose]
240: ```
241: 
242: | Path | Purpose |
243: |---|---|
244: | `[path]` | [Role] |
245: 
246: <!-- For items needing more than one line, use the itemized pattern
247:      from Section 4 instead of this table. -->
248: 
249: 
250: ---
251: 
252: ## 6. CONFIGURATION
253: 
254: | Option | Default | Purpose |
255: |---|---|---|
256: | `[OPTION]` | `[value]` | [What it controls] |
257: 
258: 
259: ---
260: 
261: ## 7. USAGE EXAMPLES
262: 
263: ```bash
264: [command]
265: ```
266: 
267: Result: [expected output or behavior].
268: 
269: 
270: ---
271: 
272: ## 8. TROUBLESHOOTING
273: 
274: | What You See | Cause | Fix |
275: |---|---|---|
276: | [Symptom] | [Cause] | [Action] |
277: 
278: 
279: ---
280: 
281: ## 9. FAQ
282: 
283: **Q: [Question readers ask often]?**
284: 
285: A: [Short answer with a link when useful.]
286: 
287: 
288: ---
289: 
290: ## 10. RELATED RESOURCES
291: 
292: ### Related Skills
293: 
294: | Skill | Relationship | Use When |
295: |---|---|---|
296: | [`[skill-name]`](../skill-name/SKILL.md) | [Sibling or dependency] | [When to use it] |
297: 
298: ### Related Documents
299: 
300: | Document | Purpose |
301: |---|---|
302: | [`[Document]`](./path/to/doc.md) | [Why it matters] |
303: 
304: ````
305: 
306: ---
307: 
308: ## 7. VALIDATION CHECKLIST
309: 
310: - [ ] README type is correct. Code folders use `readme-code-template.md`.
311: - [ ] Included sections match the audience and task.
312: - [ ] No empty sections remain.
313: - [ ] Commands were tested or marked as examples.
314: - [ ] Links use correct relative paths.
315: - [ ] Frontmatter is valid if present.
316: - [ ] No Table of Contents and no `<!-- ANCHOR -->` comments.
317: - [ ] HVR passes: no em dashes, semicolons, banned words or setup phrases.
318: 
319: ---
320: 
321: ## 8. RELATED RESOURCES
322: 
323: - [`readme-code-template.md`](./readme-code-template.md) - Code-folder README scaffold.
324: - [`SKILL.md`](../SKILL.md) - README workflow and reference map.
325: - [`core-standards.md`](../../shared/references/core-standards.md) - Markdown formatting rules.
326: - [`validation.md`](../../shared/references/validation.md) - Document validation and DQI scoring.
327: - [`hvr-rules.md`](../../sk-create-with-human-voice/references/hvr-rules.md) - Human Voice Rules.
